title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, as far as it can be inferred from pp. 72-74. P is a space. M is a set of 'pieces' X; each has a closed set |X| in P and an 'open part' (open stratum) |X|° in P. The boundary is ∂X = |X| \ |X|°, and in good cases ∂X = ⋃_{Z<X} |Z|°, where ≤ is the incidence order (Z ≤ X roughly when |Z| ⊂ |X|). Grothendieck writes Z |°| X for |Z|° ∩ |X|° = ∅ ('the open parts are disjoint') and Z ‖ X for |Z| ∩ |X| = ∅. A 'figure' is a subset of M, with |S|° = ⋃_{X∈S} |X|°. The previous page asks whether S ↦ |S|° from figures to parts of P is injective, and proposes the inverse Q ↦ s-pr°{X ∈ M : |X|° ⊂ Q}.

This page:
(1) A crossed-out start. It says the essential point is that elements of a figure F should be pairwise incomparable (X, Y ∈ F ⇒ X ≸ Y), and that F should lie in a maximal figure closed for ≤.
(2) Grothendieck then decides first to define, for a single X ∈ M, its 'open support' supp° X = A ⊂ M, and to compare it with |X|° ⊂ P.
(3) The definition can be read off from the stated equivalence: Y ∉ supp° X iff there is Z ∈ M with Z |°| X but not Z |°| Y. So supp° X = {Y : every Z whose open part misses |X|° also misses |Y|°}. This is the double polar {X}^⊥⊥ for the symmetric 'disjoint open parts' relation, i.e. the closure operator of a Birkhoff polarity / Galois connection on M.
(4) Since X ∈ supp° X, one gets |X|° ⊂ |supp° X|°. He wants equality, i.e. every Y in supp° X has |Y|° ⊂ |X|°. Contrapositively: if |Y|° ⊄ |X|°, i.e. |Y|° ∩ ∁|X|° ≠ ∅, there must exist Z with |Z|° ∩ |X|° = ∅ and |Z|° ∩ |Y|° ≠ ∅. This is a separation property of the family M.
(5) The next page finishes the argument. If |Y|° meets ∂X, take a boundary stratum Z < X. Otherwise |Y|° meets P \ |X|, and one needs the hypothesis Hyp: every point outside |X| lies in some |Z| (or |Z|°) with Z disjoint from X. He then weakens it to Z |°| X.

Purpose: to build a combinatorial/axiomatic 'analysis situs' (tame, stratified topology) in which figures in M correspond bijectively to certain unions of strata in P. supp° plays the role of a regularization: the analogue of passing from an open set to its regular-open hull ¬¬U in the Heyting algebra of opens. The desired equality |X|° = |supp° X|° says each open stratum is 'regular' with respect to the family M.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The equivalence between |X|° = |supp° X|° and '∀Y ∈ supp° X, |Y|° ⊂ |X|°' is correct, provided |A|° := ⋃_{Y∈A} |Y|°, as the context indicates.

The page leaves the needed separation property unproved. It is only established on the next page, and only under an extra hypothesis (Hyp), which Grothendieck himself immediately judges too strong and weakens.
supp° is never written down explicitly; it has to be inferred from the stated negation. If supp° were meant differently (e.g. as a 'smallest figure containing X'), the logic would need re-checking.

ideas.what: Open support supp° X of a cell X, defined as the double polar of {X} with respect to the 'disjoint open strata' relation |°|.
ideas.modern_name: Closure operator of a Galois connection / Birkhoff polarity (double orthogonal X^⊥⊥, as in orthogonality spaces and formal concept analysis); analogue of regular-open hull ¬¬U
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); regular open sets go back to Stone/Tarski; R. Wille (formal concept analysis, 1982)

ideas.what: Requiring that the open stratum |X|° be recovered from its support: |X|° = |supp° X|°.
ideas.modern_name: Regularity of strata / separation axiom for a stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (regular open sets); stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather)

ideas.what: Separation hypothesis: points outside |X| are covered by cells disjoint from X (or with disjoint open part); boundary written as ∂X = ⋃_{Z<X} |Z|° (frontier condition).
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition for stratifications plus a basis/separation axiom for the family of cells
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is announced programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5), but this combinatorial axiomatics is not developed there

ideas.what: Figures as subsets of M (antichains / ≤-closed sets) mapped to subsets |S|° of P, with injectivity of S ↦ |S|° as the goal.
ideas.modern_name: Correspondence between down-sets/antichains of the face poset and constructible unions of strata (combinatorial models of stratified spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore of face posets of regular CW / stratified spaces; recently exit-path and poset-stratified approaches (Lurie, Ayala-Francis-Tanaka)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic 'analysis situs' in which a set M of cells is governed by an abstract disjointness relation on open strata. Supports are defined as polar closures of that relation, and regularity of strata becomes a separation axiom on M. This is a polarity-theoretic (Galois-closure) route to tame/stratified topology that the 1986 notes leave as a hypothesis-hunting exercise. It does not appear developed in the tame-topology literature, which went the o-minimal route.
missed.quote: J'aimerais que l'inclusion soit vrai, i.e. que |X|° = |supp° X|° ... ∃ Z ∈ M avec Z |°| X, Z non|°| Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of mild interest. It suggests a lattice-theoretic (orthogonality-space) axiomatization of stratified spaces that could be compared with o-minimal and poset-stratified frameworks. The mathematics itself is elementary, so the value is mainly historical: documenting how Grothendieck tried to build tame topology combinatorially.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an elementary, carefully worked lemma inside an unpublished axiomatization of tame topology. Defining supports via double polars of a disjointness relation is a natural, standard device. The page is historically interesting as part of the 1986 Analysis situs project, but contains no result a specialist would find new or surprising.
transcription_corrections: Opening line: 'Je définirais d'abord' is probably 'Je vais définir d'abord' or 'Je définis d'abord', with 'vais' partly struck; the stray '$i$' is likely a colon ':'.

'(l'implication inverse étant claire)' — the image reads something like 'l'inclusion inverse étant claire' or 'l'implication inverse étant claire'. The meaning is that the reverse inclusion |X|° ⊂ |supp° X|° is clear.
'Il revient au même de dire que' is correct; the struck fragment is '$Y \notin \mathrm{supp}$' (an aborted start).

In the crossed-out block the relation is '$X \not\lessgtr Y$' (incomparable), not just '$X \not\leq Y$'. The struck text is roughly 'i.e. que F soit contenu dans une figure (chacune telles que puissent être une figure maximale, i.e. fermée pour ≤)'.
Page header '73' and archive page '82' (bottom left) are correctly placed; 'supp°' is written 's-pr°' / 'supp°' in Grothendieck's hand.
